\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تذبذب} (tazabzub)}{تذبذب (tazabzub)}]{\ur{تذبذب} (tazabzub) — indecision; wavering}

\label{lesson:UR-C538-tazabzub}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a touchstone, then the Urdu for to select.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تذبذب}}
\textbf{\ur{تذبذب}} — \emph{tazabzub} — \textquotedblleft{}indecision; wavering\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{تذبذب} \ur{میں} \ur{ہیں} \ur{تو} \ur{کل} \ur{بتائیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp tazabzub meṅ haiṅ to kal batāiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you can't decide, let me know tomorrow.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تذبذب}} (\emph{tazabzub}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{tadhabdhub}, \textquotedblleft{}dangling to and fro\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tazabzub}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tazabzub}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āp tazabzub meṅ haiṅ to kal batāiye.} — If you can't decide, let me know tomorrow.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a touchstone, then the Urdu for to select, then say \emph{tazabzub} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{تذبذب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Indecision; wavering\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{متردد} (mutaraddid)}{متردد (mutaraddid)}]{\ur{متردد} (mutaraddid) — hesitant; in doubt}

\label{lesson:UR-C538-mutaraddid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to select, then the Urdu for indecision.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{متردد}}
\textbf{\ur{متردد}} — \emph{mutaraddid} — \textquotedblleft{}hesitant; in doubt\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar voh mutaraddid hai to ham intizār kareṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ur{متردد}} (\emph{mutaraddid}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{mutaraddid}, \textquotedblleft{}going back and forth\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گمان} (gumān)}{گمان (gumān)}]{\ur{گمان} (gumān) — a hunch; a notion}

\label{lesson:UR-C538-guman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for indecision, then the Urdu for hesitant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گمان}}
\textbf{\ur{گمان}} — \emph{gumān} — \textquotedblleft{}a hunch; a notion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{میرا} \ur{گمان} \ur{ٹھیک} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{وہ} \ur{کل} \ur{آئے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar merā gumān ṭhīk hai to voh kal āe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If my hunch is right, he will come tomorrow.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گمان}} (\emph{gumān}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{gumān}, \textquotedblleft{}a supposition, a doubt\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ڈگمگانا} (ḍagmagānā)}{ڈگمگانا (ḍagmagānā)}]{\ur{ڈگمگانا} (ḍagmagānā) — to totter; to wobble}

\label{lesson:UR-C538-dagmagana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for hesitant, then the Urdu for a hunch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ڈگمگانا}}
\textbf{\ur{ڈگمگانا}} — \emph{ḍagmagānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to totter; to wobble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{سیڑھی} \ur{ڈگمگائی} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{گر} \ur{جاؤں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar sīṛhī ḍagmagāī to maiṅ gir jāūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the ladder wobbles, I will fall.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{بوڑھا} \ur{آدمی} \ur{ڈگمگایا}, \emph{voh būṛhā ādmī ḍagmagāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ڈگمگانا}} (\emph{ḍagmagānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousins \emph{ḍagmagḍagānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to tremble\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{ḍigmig}, \textquotedblleft{}trembling\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*ḍag}, \textquotedblleft{}tremble\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5522).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for hesitant, then the Urdu for a hunch, then say \emph{ḍagmagānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اٹل} (aṭal)}{اٹل (aṭal)}]{\ur{اٹل} (aṭal) — unshakable; immovable}

\label{lesson:UR-C538-atal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a hunch, then the Urdu for to totter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اٹل}}
\textbf{\ur{اٹل}} — \emph{aṭal} — \textquotedblleft{}unshakable; immovable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{میرا} \ur{ارادہ} \ur{اٹل} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{کوئی} \ur{نہیں} \ur{روک} \ur{سکتا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar merā irādā aṭal hai to koī nahīṅ rok saktā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If my mind is made up, nobody can stop me.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اٹل}} (\emph{aṭal}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{aṭala}, \textquotedblleft{}not shaky, firm\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a hunch, then the Urdu for to totter, then say \emph{aṭal} again
